Hi Sanjay & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time to meet today — really appreciated the context on Acme's support KB and the multi-source docs you mentioned. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side so we can kick off the RAG eval you asked for: 

Summary & recommendations
- Recommended model(s): start with Redwood-2.7B-q4 for initial cost/latency baseline; if you need higher recall/longer context, evaluate Redwood-13B and an optional >70B variant for edge-case fidelity.
- Retrieval settings: use Redwood-embed-3 for dense vectors, initial k=10 with MMR tuning (lambda=0.7).
- Reranker choice: test both our light-weight reranker (low-latency, recall-focused) and the cross-encoder (higher precision, higher latency). See attached reranker_options.pdf.
- Grounding & metrics: we'll run grounding metrics including source coverage, grounding score (percentage of answers with at least one top-3 source), and factuality regressions versus your baseline.

Deliverables we propose
1) 10k-doc RAG eval run (ingest, index, run prompt set v2) — includes benchmark CSV and prompt-set attached.
2) Benchmark report: latency, token cost, grounding metrics, reranker precision/recall tradeoffs.
3) Short recommended config (retriever+reranker+model) and estimated cost delta.

Proposed timeline
- Confirm scope & docs to include: by Fri 9/17
- Tech kickoff (30–45m) with Dylan: week of 9/20
- Eval run & initial results: 1 week after kickoff

Next steps for you
- Please confirm which document sources to include (Sanjay: is the Confluence dump + S3 bucket the full set?), and whether you want us to include logs/search queries in the eval.
- If OK, I’ll schedule the tech kickoff (Dylan will lead) and share the eval plan + sample prompt set.

Hi Sanjay / Priya — happy to answer those: 

Grounding metrics (how we compute)
- Grounding score: percent of generated answers where at least one of the top-3 retrieved passages is cited in the final answer. We report top-1, top-3 coverage and an attribution precision metric (how often the claimed source actually supports the answer).
- Factuality regressions: we run an NLI-based factuality check + heuristics against known QA pairs where available.

Reranker / latency tradeoffs
- Light-weight reranker (token-light cross-encoder distilled model): ~60–120ms extra latency per request on our p3-like instances for k<=10; typically keeps end-to-end within 300–450ms depending on model size.
- Full cross-encoder: higher precision but adds ~200–350ms at k=10 on the same hardware. If 400ms median is a hard SLO, we recommend testing the light-weight reranker first with k=8 and caching top results for repeated queries.

Retrieval & model specifics (proposed first pass)
- Embeddings: Redwood-embed-3 (dense), 768-d vectors, cosine similarity, initial k=10.
- Indexing: FAISS HNSW with efSearch tuned for recall.
- Models: Redwood-2.7B-q4 baseline; Redwood-13B as a lift; optional >70B for high-fidelity failcases.

Benchmark artifacts attached: acme_rag_benchmark_results.csv (template) and a short note on reranker tradeoffs. I’ll also upload our sample eval scripts to the Drive link Marissa included.

If you want, we can run a quick latency sweep (2k queries) to validate the 400ms median for your expected qps before ingesting the full 10k docs.

-Dylan
